taxonomic_note: Hydrocotyle bonariensis Comm. ex Lam. is accepted by Kew POWO. Crucial: Kew currently treats the older name H. verticillata var. triradiata (A.Rich.) Fernald as a synonym of H. bonariensis, although some Texas manuals and local UT treatments continue using H. verticillata var. triradiata. This is an authentic disagreement among sources. Do not silently rewrite H. verticillata, treat photos labeled var. triradiata as verified bonariensis, or declare local native provenance without reviewing vouchers and BONAP county maps.
look_here_first: DON'T USE THE ROUND LEAVES TO SPECIES-ID. Find the WHOLE FLOWERING STALK. Largeleaf/dune pennywort has a COMPOUND, proliferating inflorescence: a long main flowering peduncle terminates in a primary umbel of several rays, AND those rays themselves carry whorls of little flowers or fruits along their length—like tiny branching miniature whorled stems. Compare H. umbellata (mostly one crowded simple terminal many-flowered cluster) and H. verticillata (interrupted whorls largely arranged along a single main flowering axis). Capture the primary BRANCH POINT plus an entire secondary ray; any ambiguous or sterile specimen stays Hydrocotyle sp. or a cautious species complex.

best_field_traits: Creeping perennial rhizomatous wetland/sandy-ground herb rooting at nodes, with many erect petioles and round leaves elevated above the substrate.

Large orbicular or slightly kidney-rounded PELTATE leaves; the petiole inserts on the UNDERSIDE within the perimeter rather than into an open basal sinus. Shallow crenate/scalloped margins and palmate veins radiate from insertion point.
Reproductive stalk is typically LONGER than associated leaf petiole, ending in a branching PROLIFEROUS / COMPOUND umbel rather than a single crowd of little white flowers.

In a well-developed flowering stalk, ~5–7 primary rays diverge near the tip, and EACH RAY can elongate into its own verticillate flowering axis with several spaced little rings of flowers/fruits. Look for more than one secondary branch.
Five very small whitish to cream petals on individual flowers; observe delicate thread-like pedicels rather than interpreting small round green buds as fruit without a close-up.

Mature flattened oval-to-ellipsoid schizocarps break into paired one-seeded mericarps; base often cordate (heart-shaped notch) with pronounced dorsal/lateral ribs and a longish style, but final fruit ID needs a macro and scale.
Under an alternate taxonomy, some Texas plants named H. verticillata var. triradiata fall within bonariensis at Kew. Older name and source photos require extra voucher scrutiny.
morphology_keys.habit: Glabrous to nearly hairless perennial with slender rooting stolons/rhizomes; may form broad vegetative mats in moist sandy soils, dune depressions, wetlands, ditches, and intermittently saturated edges.
morphology_keys.leaf_arrangement: Alternate on runners; foliage from closely spaced stem nodes can look rosetted.
morphology_keys.leaf: Simple peltate approximately circular blades, shallowly crenate/scalloped and palmately veined; sources often describe ~3–8 cm diameter, but size variable and strongly overlapping with other Hydrocotyle, so not a sole key.
morphology_keys.petiole: Long, round slender stalk fastened centrally or subcentrally beneath the blade. Typical botanical references describe petioles around 7–20 cm, sometimes much longer.
morphology_keys.leaf_attachment: Peltate: show underside of round blade where petiole physically connects within margin. Top-side vein radiations alone are not a fully verified underside photograph.
morphology_keys.stem: Creeping rhizomes running at or below soil surface, with fine roots from nodes. To document, gently lift a rooted section and photograph several connected nodes without unnecessary habitat disturbance.
morphology_keys.inflorescence: Proliferous, compound, umbel-derived axis: primary long peduncle ends in an umbel with multiple primary rays, each developing separated verticillate flower or fruit tiers. Kew POWO general information (Flora Zambesiaca) explicitly describes ~5–7 rays and each ray becoming a verticillate raceme.
morphology_keys.reproductive_stalk: The whole flower axis generally longer than subtending leaf petiole. A photo of the terminal head only CANNOT confirm compound branching; reveal the main umbel branchpoint and distal secondary rays.
morphology_keys.flowers: Tiny, bisexual white to cream 5-petaled flowers; slender pedicels (1–20 mm reported in Flora Zambesiaca concept), whorled with slender acute bracteoles subtending flower clusters.
morphology_keys.fruit: Laterally flattened ellipsoid schizocarps with paired mericarps; base cordate and ribs often prominent, mature fruit reddish-brown or slightly wrinkled. Require millimeter scale and true botanical orientation before labeling ribs/styles.
morphology_keys.habitat: Coastal dune slacks and wet sand are particularly typical; also marsh depressions and intermittently flooded ponds/ditches. Texas state-level native distribution per Kew; this does not establish inland Hays County occurrence.
morphology_keys.season: Generally flowers in warmer moist months, but vary by locale; no unsupported Hays County seasonal guarantee.
morphology_keys.field_caution: H. umbellata, H. verticillata, H. bonariensis can look like the same plant if photographed leaf-only; fertile whole axes and well-identified specimens are essential.

field_comparison_matrix.key_feature: COMPOUND umbel. Primary rays spread, then become secondary axes with individual spaced flower/fruit whorls.
field_comparison_matrix.shared_leaf: Circular peltate scalloped leaf; similar to other pennyworts
field_comparison_matrix.confidence: Branchpoint plus separate whorled secondary axis is strongest teaching target; fruit needed in ambiguous plants

field_comparison_matrix.key_feature: Mostly SIMPLE, crowded terminal cluster with 15–35+ small flowers; rare extra tiers.
field_comparison_matrix.confidence: Scan whole flower axis; one head can mislead

field_comparison_matrix.key_feature: Small discrete whorls arranged along an interrupted spike/raceme; pedicels often shorter, axes may rarely branch.
field_comparison_matrix.confidence: Kew synonymizes historical var. triradiata with H. bonariensis. Plant voucher/ray branch pattern required.

field_comparison_matrix.key_feature: Peltate false: deeply notched leaf with petiole joined at OPEN basal sinus; floating habit common.
field_comparison_matrix.confidence: Photograph underside/base of a leaf; no guess by habitat alone

field_comparison_matrix.key_feature: Kidney-shaped or crenate blade, petiole attached at BASAL notch rather than peltate center; tiny low flower groups.
Non-peltate kidney blade, small hidden umbels, provenance uncertain in inland native zone.
Kidney leaf with entire smooth margin and petiole at edge notch; solitary tiny greenish cup flowers, not branched umbels.
Nonpeltate mostly entire leaves; tiny solitary flower, fruit stalk recurved near tip.
OPPOSITE leaves and raised lilac-white flower button; no peltate circular leaf.
OPPOSITE toothed leaves and yellow composite heads.

crew_quick_key: 1. Round leaf? Prove peltate petiole insertion by flipping one whole blade. If not, check Centella, Dichondra or H. ranunculoides.
2. Follow complete reproductive axis: one crowded dense upper flower group → H. umbellata.
3. One main axis with separated, small flower rings → investigate H. verticillata.
4. Several PRIMARY rays branching, EACH carrying more little flower/fruit rings along its own axis → investigate H. bonariensis.
5. When flower axes are incomplete or historical var. triradiata labels appear, retain Hydrocotyle sp. / taxonomic HOLD until a measured reproductive collection settles it.
comparisons.warning: Branching can occur in more than one Hydrocotyle, and historical varieties are not aligned across floras. This three-way key is a teaching heuristic, not a guarantee of correct species for all Texas populations.

family_genus_teaching.family: Araliaceae (order Apiales); some older keys place Hydrocotyle within Apiaceae. Flowers very small with five free petals and an inferior ovary; ripe fruit a flattened schizocarp comprising two one-seeded mericarps.
family_genus_teaching.genus: Hydrocotyle: creeping wet or sandy-ground herbs, round often peltate leaves and tiny umbels/verticils; fruit/reproductive branching stronger for species than leaf diameter.
family_genus_teaching.species: H. bonariensis: the key feature is a compound, branching proliferous umbel with primary rays whose distal portions carry whorls of separate flowers/fruits.
family_genus_teaching.crew_question: Can you show the junction of the MAIN flower stalk into multiple RAYS, then a ray bearing its own separated flower/fruit whorls? If not, don't force bonariensis.

ecological_notes.native_range: Texas is in Kew's state/native range; BONAP/NAPA Hays County and target western counties NOT screened. Status remains unresolved; no native-score inclusion.
ecological_notes.habitat: Commonly wet coastal sand/dune slack species but also on marshy or periodically flooded margins; habitat information from regional botanical guides, not proof of inland local occurrence.
ecological_notes.management: Potential low creeping cover; avoid introducing unconfirmed inland coastal provenance into conservation restoration until target-area native evidence and source genetics are checked.
ecological_notes.host_insects: No species-specific Lepidoptera or specialist bee scores verified, do not invent them.

diagnostic_photo_requirements.needed: Main flowering stalk branching into primary rays with SECONDARY whorled axes visibly attached.
Same-scale photographs of true compound branching versus interrupted simple whorled spike; source taxonomy verified.
Flip leaf, show petiole joining underside away from blade margin and radiating veins.
Ripe schizocarp with two flattened mericarps, rib profile and scale in mm.
Peltate leaf habitat, rooting rhizome/node evidence.
Macro of 5-petaled blossoms and narrow flower pedicels; separate calyx from petal.
